verdict.tagline: Endless social worlds driven by user creation, plagued by technical friction and toxicity.
for_you_if: you seek boundless social spaces to explore with friends
you stick to private lobbies to avoid public toxicity
you enjoy discovering user-created worlds and avatars
not_for_you_if: you want stable performance in virtual reality mode
you expect robust content moderation in public spaces
you refuse to pay for age verification features

claims.claim: Reviewers note the presence of toxic behavior, harassment, and offensive language such as racial slurs in public spaces.

citations.review_text:
I never write reviews for games but I want to give my input. When I played VRChat back in like, maybe 2018 (I currently play primarily on VR so I don't have a lot of hours on my pc), it was so much fun and less toxic compared to now days. Derogatory slurs to POC/Queer individuals, harassment both on a cyberbullying level or inappropriately and just generally more annoying individuals like trolls or people who just have no respect for others personal spaces, interests or comfortability. This game *can* be fun, but you really need to find your group of people and if you're not the offensive type intentionally or for dark humor, then your chances of finding people to hang out with are slim unless you know where to look before hand.
If you get easily offended or any mental disorders like depression or anxiety, I strongly suggest either coming into this game with extreme caution or just avoiding it all together and that isn't to be rude... It's really bad.

These issues probably wont ever be fixed because the moderation from what I've heard is garbage, which is probably why its such a rampant issue because they know they can get away with it lol.

If you already have a group of friends, I do recommend playing it, but doing friends/invite only worlds or worlds who are strictly moderated. Which is the only reason why I'm giving this game a thumbs up, because like I said, it *can* be fun, it's just so damn specific...

BAD: Kids screaming racial slurs, weird E-couples.
good: Really cool skin to try, and play with THE BOYZZ

i saw a  trans furry call someone the n word 


10/10 would witness racism again

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game is significantly better and more enjoyable when played with friends or in private lobbies compared to public spaces.

citations.review_text: It's really fun when you have a group of friends playing together. It can be an interesting place to meet others, but beware the underage children that are scattered around. VR Chat is really a neutral place for all ages to gather, you just need to find your own niche.

Great to play with friends, not by yourself.

Keep that in mind

Was forced to play this game with a few friends (unfortunately several times)

But after joining a public server once, I am glad to stick to the friends only lobbies (^-^;)
Fun with friends. Thats really the point of the game. Is best with vr.
Great game the communities is nice to me and my friends made so much memories on the way I highly recommend this game. Just avoid the trolls and the weird people.

I'm going to start this off by saying that this review has absolutely nothing to do with anything in public instances. I've been avoiding those for as long as I've been playing. I play with friends in invite-only intances exclusively, and for that this game is perfect.
I'm leaving a negative review because ♥♥♥♥ MANDATORY AGE VERIFICATION. If I'm forced to give up my privacy and anonymity to access certain content, I will simply leave the game entirely. I don't *want* to, but the truth is there are alternatives that I could absolutely migrate to, and if it comes to that, I will.
Most the player bass is wired. So yeah, I'll just stay in my private worlds.
Its a fun game I enjoyed playing with friends and being what and who I want but it is filled with racist people and everyone swears for no reason so I stay in a private lobby so I don't hear racism

This game might as well be the definition of Your Mileage May Vary. You either have the absolute worst time with it, or have a pretty good time with it. It's a blast with friends, but do be weary of public servers...
...or so I hear. A good chunk of my playtime is exclusively with friends.

It is a good game don't get me wrong, but it's 100 times better with friends. Public lobbys are alright, but it's better with friends. But i recommend this for people 13+ who wanna play in private lobbys or with friends.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from poor performance and low frame rates in virtual reality mode.

citations.review_text: I average 45fps on SteamVR on Vrchat, Played it for well over 2000 Hours on meta and around 500 Hours on Steam as i make this review, I have made so many friends thanks to vrchat, and i would say this game has helped me talk to new people not just in game but in real life, I was pretty socially awkward before this

VRChat is a mixed bag. 
It can be looked from different angles and the outcome can vary a lot. From one angle, this game is where you can create and share impressive, visually stunning characters with absolutely incredible features, I am getting surprised what is possible in this era of gaming almost every time I go there. And the fact that it can be used in VR mode is just one more reason why I think it can be just an incredible experience, whether users have just basic VR kit, or something more advanced, such as full body tracking, or even face tracking (eyes and mouth).
And then, we look from different angles, and we can see: horribly optimized game (even with decent rig, I might struggle to keep FPS in VR above 30 in certain areas even when the shown avatar count is set to low), or the overall limitations of the engine (the parameter count limit - those who make avatars in Unity will know), the ones responsible for "running" this platform and their decisions, TOS, monetization, age verification and validation are ... "questionable" to say the least (plus the fact that without community making content, their game is basically a hollow shell). And of course the community - you can meet the weirdest weirdos, or the most amazing people (just like in real life, who would have guessed?)
This game is truly incredible experience, one of a kind - the concept of the game is incredible, but it has its flaws.

I saw a review that says this game is basically VR Roblox, and yeah, that hits the nail on the head. There's some goodies in it, but for all intents and purposes, the good is outweighed by the bad. It may not be the loftsided 10:90 some people try to make it, but in my experience id say Good:Bad its like 43:57.

The game also runs pretty poorly in VR, even with an optimized avatar. This isn't entirely VRChats fault, as a lot of lag comes from *other* peoples avatars, but the fact i can barely hit 90 FPS on the *home world* on the lowest settings doesn't really help. Sure, my PC isn't exactly a VR Powerhouse, but it should still be able to keep up. and hate me if ya want, im not blowing 500 bones on 16 more gb of RAM.  At that point it'd be better to just get the steam frame and run that standalone.

I've mainly played on PC and my Specs have changed throughout my time playing from a gaming laptop to a mid-teir gaming pc to now with a semi-high teir pc and no matter what it's been playable in PC mode. in VR mode it seems to be a mess with it barely playing via the link cable. dispite this I still reccomend this as the people you will meet vary a bunch and there's infinite adventure to be had. the moderation of avatars is a bit wonky and not the best so expect to randomly lose a avatar or two.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe disconnect issues and repetitive navigation steps required to rejoin game sessions after losing connection.

citations.review_text:
Every update has progressively made it harder for me to play since I tend to disconnect. At first I could just rejoin in a matter of seconds, now i have to disconnect twice in a row and get sent back to the default vrc world before i can rejoin which usually requires me to get an invite back, and it happens consistently.
The game itself is also nearly unbearable in public instances.

I don't know about any other pc player's having this issue, but whenever I try to look around it bugs my entire game out and my pc is built to handle huge games. No matter what game I join in vrchat I always have the issue which mean it's not the game I join, it's vrchat. 
As I said, I have no idea if anyone else has had this problem but it's so bad to the point I cannot play the game. I have never had this issue before until all these updates came into place.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the community features many toxic individuals, including trolls, racists, and people screaming slurs.

citations.review_text: If you're looking for a game that personifies the internet, look no further than VRchat. It's got it all, from the racist and sexist to the wholesome. You'll find just about every kind of person on here, if you spend enough time on it.
this games fun until someone spams n word

With the wave of age verification specially with it locked behind a one time payment of VRChat+ it has brought out a whole new wave of narcissistic, cringy, elitist scum that make VrChat as bad as all its haters say it is.

If your here to meet people to try to help with social issues then try to find groups in discords or something as open worlds are playgrounds for some of these scum of the planet to just be horrible people, or the kids running around in avatars that are naked and made to crash the game or even the PC screaming slurs at the top of their little annoying lungs. Which will make you wonder why their parents haven't come in and slapped them upside the head...

But once in a very great while you may find one or two people that are generally good people that introduce you to groups that will open Vrchat to a whole new place of friends becoming like family... just for them to turn against you or use you until they are done with you then kick you to a curb like a used cond.. umm yea you get the picture i hope.

Vrchat was once a great idea for people to get together to have fun, throw parties and meet people from all over the world. To learn things to be part of something. Now its just a cesspit of deranged, narcissist, elitist, that thank they get to do what ever they want because they paid $10 once upon a time to prove they are "adults". 

I'm glade i got to meet a few genuinely great people that i still can call friends  but i wouldn't recommend Vrchat unless you are already know some people that already play it. Also you don't need high end headsets or FBT( full body tracking) as some will tell you, Start off small just use the pc desktop version then maybe a quest before you think about going all in on something like the Index with tracking pucks for full body.
so honestly the game is really fun if you just dont pay attention to the people who scream slurs and other stuff just make friends a block the bad ones.

citations.review_text: This game solely relies on it's playerbase for content. All of the content made is mostly user-created which does open doors for creative people but with how late and mid the moderation is, I would say it's not worth it to allow just any user to make avatars and worlds for the platform. Also VRChat has pushing out more FOMO slop for 30 every month not including everything else that's present in the store. Also this game is friendslop because all the games are either made by Jar or badly designed not to mention the unreasonable amount of competitive people. Also all of the "beautiful" worlds that are recommended are filled with post-processing, god-rays, and yandere-dev level modelling. Only reason why I play this game is to larp
